contracts.title: Open Framework - Residential Care for children with multiple presenting needs (Phase 2b)
contracts.description:
Nottinghamshire County Council (the Council) is seeking to establish an Open Framework of suitable Providers to deliver residential care for children with multiple presenting needs, which includes those children displaying sexualised behaviours, on a planned and emergency basis.

Ideally the support offered within this Framework will be delivered in Nottinghamshire for both emergency and planned packages of care. This will enable children to be supported by the Health and Education offer. In some cases, there may be a reason for the child to be supported outside of the county. For Providers delivering care outside of Nottinghamshire we will consider homes that are within a 30-mile radius of the county border. Providers of services for children displaying harmful sexual behaviours are exempt from this.

A multi-provider framework agreement will be put in place which means that during the framework term the Council may re-open the Residential Care for children with multiple presenting needs (Phase 2b) tender exercise to run further competitive processes to allow new providers to be appointed to the Framework.

The initial framework agreement will be in place for 2 years, from 1st September 2026 to 31st August 2028.
Further framework agreements may then be in place for a maximum of 8 years in total (2+2+2), until 31st August 2034.

Bidders should ensure they have fully reviewed all supporting tender documents before submitting their application.

Please note that this framework is not for the provision of supported accommodation.

contracts.title: Bus Shelter Advertising Extension
contracts.description:
Nottinghamshire County Council has extended its existing concession agreement for bus shelter advertising by three years to support the transition of transport functions to EMCCA is completed. 

Nottinghamshire County Council (the Council) maintains in excess of 4,500 bus stops with 1,483 bus shelters and almost 1,200 real time displays. Since 2000, the Incumbent Provider has supplied and maintained 470 of the 1,483 bus shelters in Nottinghamshire at no cost to the Council in exchange for selling advertising space on approximately 45% of their shelters and retaining ownership of each bus shelter it supplies under the contract. This represents excellent value to the Council as it would cost over £6.5 million to install like for like shelters and £50k per annum to clean and maintain them.

Since 2019, the Incumbent Provider started replacing its paper advertising with digital advertising and the Council negotiated a contract variation to receive an income for every digital panel added to the Incumbent Provider's estate. The Incumbent Provider currently have 30 such panels, with the income used to offset the Council's bus stop infrastructure maintenance costs. The Incumbent Provider supplies and has maintained its shelter estate to a high standard, and it remains in good condition.

The current contract for delivery of the bus shelter advertising will expire on 1 May 2025, and it has been in place for 25 years.

The Council's Local Transport Authority functions will transfer to the East Midlands Combined County Authority (EMCCA) on or before 31st March 2026. At present it is unclear whether bus shelters owned by the Council will transfer or contracts such as that held between the Council and the Incumbent Provider will be novated by this date or at all. There is also expected to be a considerable period of adjustment within EMCCA as the Transport team beds in and the functions to support delivery mature.

contracts.title: Nottinghamshire Healthy Families Programme 2025
contracts.description:
Nottinghamshire County Council is seeking a single Provider to deliver an early intervention and prevention public health nursing service delivering health visiting and school nursing services in line with the Governments Healthy Child Programme (HCP).
Bidders MUST be CQC registered and will have delivered public health nursing services in scope of this requirement within the last 5 years. They must have demonstrated continuous improvement in service delivery and have provided clinical and operational leadership where they operate.

The contract will operate for an initial term of three years with an option to extend for up to a further two years in one 24 month increment.

The primary aim of the service, as further described in the Specification and Specification Appendices, will be to support parents and carers to give children the best start in life, keeping their children healthy and safe and enabling them to reach their full potential.

It will be delivered by multi-disciplinary Healthy Family Teams working in close partnership with the children's health, care, and early help system. It will be a universal service for all Nottinghamshire children, young people and their families aged 0 to 19 who are resident or attending school in Nottinghamshire. This will extend to children and young people aged under 25 where there are special education needs and disabilities.

The Nottinghamshire Healthy Families Programme will include the delivery of:

• Health visiting and school nursing services,
• Mandated health and development reviews for children from 0 to 5,
• The national child measurement programme (NCMP),
• An early intervention offer for parents with additional vulnerabilities, and
• The family nurse partnership programme.

We invite Providers to review the attached tender documentation and submit bids accordingly.

contracts.description: Nottinghamshire County Council is seeking a medical assessor (Provider) to provide medical assessments for existing and potential foster carers to support the foster care application process. Detailed requirements are set out in the service specification. Local authorities have a statutory duty to provide sufficient accommodation for Looked After Children. This is challenging as sufficiency of foster care and residential care placements has been identified as an issue nationally. Any delays to reviews and applications of foster carers compounds this issue, both locally and nationally. Nottinghamshire County Council aims to address local sufficiency challenges in foster carers, in part by recruiting additional foster carers into the local authority. As part of the recruitment process, foster cares undergo and assessment by a medical practitioner. This assessment has previously been carried out by the foster carer's GP. However, due to Covid-19, GP practices are operating at and beyond capacity, this is delaying and preventing new foster carers coming into the foster care system, and existing foster carers from having reviews. The aim of the service is to improve sufficiency in foster carers by supporting the recruitment of new foster carers, and the review of existing foster carers. Medical assessments are required for the following cohorts - • New potential foster carers to support their applications • Existing foster carers where reviews are required • 'Connected carers' where the foster carer has a relationship to the child • Foster carers wishing to care for children under a Special Guardianship Order As a fostering agency, Nottinghamshire County Council are expected to have a medical advisor . , All foster carers should have a medical as part of their assessment process and their 3-yearly review The contract will have an initial duration of 36 months with an option to extend with a further 12 months.

The aim of the service is to assist/enable children to move towards a safer and more settled lifestyle and recover from sexual exploitation and/or sexual abuse by:  
?	increasing the number of children at risk of, or victim to CSE, accessing quality support
?	reducing the number of children experiencing CSE in Nottinghamshire through preventative strategies
?	increasing the numbers of children identified at an earlier stage
?	providing therapeutic services to minimise the effects of abuse / exploitation on mental health and emotional well-being
?	promoting resilience and reduce vulnerability to further abuse

contracts.title: PROVISION OF ORAL-FLUID DRUG TESTING PRODUCTS AND LABORATORY ANALYSIS
contracts.description:
Nottinghamshire County Council (?the Council?) is seeking competitive quotes for the provision of oral-fluid drug testing products and laboratory analysis for use across Nottinghamshire?s Children?s Social Case Service

Nottinghamshire County Council?s Children?s Social Care Service is involved with an increasing number of parents and carers where there are concerns around substance misuse. This is impacting on a considerable number of children and young people, of whom a significant proportion are subject to Child Protection Plans. A need has therefore been identified for point-of-care oral-fluid testing of parents / carers of children and young people who are open to Children?s Social Care. This is for the purpose of effective safeguarding, as well as decision-making in relation to the welfare of the child or young person

While the oral-fluid drug tests will be undertaken during home visits by social workers within Nottinghamshire?s District Child Protection Teams, the Authority will need to purchase oral-fluid swabs from the provider. Social workers will also need to be effectively trained to undertake oral-fluid tests, to ensure that there is no break in the chain of custody in the event that the result is required as evidence in court. In conjunction with this, the Council will require laboratory analysis of the oral-fluid tests undertaken by social workers, to test for a broad drugs library, with a timely return of results.

The price submitted must be for the unit costs of oral-fluid swab purchases, the training of social workers within Nottinghamshire?s District Child Protection Teams and the laboratory analysis of a broad drugs library. Where appropriate, this may include costs for the testing of standard drug libraries, as well as additional costs for the testing of particular substances.
